events.title: The First Council of Nicaea opens
events.shortBlurb: The first ecumenical council of the Church gathered at Nicaea under the Emperor Constantine to answer the Arian denial of Christ’s divinity, and gave the Church its Creed…
body: The first ecumenical council of the Church opened at Nicaea in Bithynia on 20 May 325, summoned by the Emperor Constantine in the year after he had reunited the empire under his sole rule. By the traditional count of Athanasius 318 bishops attended, many bearing the scars of the late persecutions; Pope Sylvester I sent two priest-legates.

The council met chiefly to answer the Alexandrian priest Arius, who taught that the Son was a creature, not co-eternal with the Father. Against him the fathers confessed the Son to be 'consubstantial with the Father' — homoousios — and the creed they framed, expanded at Constantinople in 381, is still sung at Mass.

Nicaea also established a common reckoning for the date of Easter, legislated for the Meletian schism in Egypt, and issued twenty canons of discipline. Arius was condemned and exiled to Illyricum; the sessions ended in the late summer of 325.

sources.text: Catholic Encyclopedia (1913), “The First Council of Nicaea”

events.title: Ignatius of Loyola is wounded at Pamplona
events.shortBlurb: A cannonball shattered the leg of a Spanish soldier and set in motion the conversion that gave the Church the Jesuits…
body: On 20 May 1521, in the defense of the citadel of Pamplona against a French army, a cannonball shattered one leg of the Basque captain Íñigo López de Loyola and grievously wounded the other. The garrison soon surrendered; the victors, admiring his courage, set his bones and sent him home to the castle of Loyola.

The convalescence was long and bitter — the badly set leg was broken and reset — and, finding no romances in the house, he read the Life of Christ by Ludolph of Saxony and the Golden Legend of Jacobus de Voragine. Their pages moved him to exchange the service of an earthly king for the service of God.

From that sickbed came the vigil at Montserrat, the year of prayer at Manresa where the Spiritual Exercises took shape, the vows at Montmartre in 1534 with six companions, and the approval of the Society of Jesus by Pope Paul III in 1540. The Jesuits have ever reckoned their beginning from that wound.
